description: A gem factory has two drills, a high intensity one and a low intensity one. Each day, the high intensity drill can process 50 gems and requires 50 units of water to dissipate heat. Each day, the low intensity drill can process 30 gems and requires 20 units of water to dissipate heat. Each day the factory must process 800 gems and they have available 700 units of water. Since the high intensity drill produces a lot of noise pollution, at most 40% of the drills can be high intensity ones. Further, at least 10 should be low intensity drills. How many of each drill should be used to minimize the total number of drills needed?

GemsPerHigh.definition: Number of gems processed per day by a high intensity drill.

WaterPerHigh.definition: Units of water required per day to dissipate heat by a high intensity drill.

GemsPerLow.definition: Number of gems processed per day by a low intensity drill.

WaterPerLow.definition: Units of water required per day to dissipate heat by a low intensity drill.

TotalGems.definition: Total number of gems that must be processed per day by the factory.

AvailableWater.definition: Total units of water available per day for dissipating heat.

MaxHighFraction.definition: Maximum fraction of drills that can be high intensity to limit noise pollution.

MinLowDrills.definition: Minimum number of low intensity drills that must be used.

objective.description: "Minimize the total number of drills used (high intensity plus low intensity) per day."

HighDrills.definition: Number of high intensity drills used per day

LowDrills.definition: Number of low intensity drills used per day
